title: September 2019 Class Block 3 Supplementary College Final Exam (Part 4 of 6)
unit: Comprehensive Nursing (Neurology, Orthopaedics, Dermatology, Gastroenterology, Perioperative Nursing, Pharmacology, Paediatrics, Infectious Diseases)

sets.title: Set 1: Original Exam Questions
sets.description: The original MCQs from the September 2019 class Block 3 Supplementary College Final Exam paper (Kenya Registered Nursing, sat 6 December 2022, Multiple Choice Questions, Q61 to Q80).

questions.text: The nurse notes the patient’s face droops on one side. The nurse suspects injury to cranial nerve:
questions.explanation: VII (C) is correct because the facial nerve supplies the muscles of facial expression, so injury or paralysis (for example Bell's palsy or stroke) causes drooping of one side of the face, an inability to close the eye, smile or raise the eyebrow, and loss of taste on the front of the tongue. IV (A) is incorrect because the trochlear nerve supplies the superior oblique muscle of the eye, and injury causes double vision when looking downwards. V (B) is incorrect because the trigeminal nerve carries sensation from the face and supplies the muscles of chewing. X (D) is incorrect because the vagus nerve supplies the pharynx, larynx and the thoracic and abdominal organs, and injury causes hoarseness, difficulty in swallowing and a deviated uvula.

questions.text: A complication of fracture characterized by pale appearance of the extremity, cold skin, delayed capillary refill and paresthesia is:
questions.explanation: Compartment syndrome (C) is correct because swelling or bleeding inside a closed fascial compartment raises the pressure and cuts off the blood supply and the nerves, which produces the classic signs of pain out of proportion to the injury (the earliest sign), pallor, a cold limb, delayed capillary refill, paresthesia, pulselessness and paralysis (the 'six Ps'). It is an emergency treated by loosening the cast or bandages and by urgent fasciotomy. Deep venous thrombosis (A) is incorrect because it causes calf swelling, warmth, redness and tenderness. Fat embolism (B) is incorrect because it appears 24 to 72 hours after a long bone fracture with respiratory distress, confusion and petechiae over the chest and axillae. Heterotopic ossification (D) is incorrect because it is the later formation of bone in soft tissue around a joint, with pain and reduced movement.

questions.text: The most common cause of osteomyelitis is:
questions.explanation: Staphylococcus aureus (A) is correct because it causes about 60 to 90% of cases of bone infection, spreading through the blood from a boil or skin infection, from an open fracture or wound, or from surgery. Clostridium welchii (B) is incorrect because it causes gas gangrene in deep contaminated wounds. Streptococcus hemolyticus (C) is incorrect because it mainly causes sore throat, cellulitis and rheumatic fever, and is a less common cause of bone infection. Escherichia coli (D) is incorrect because it mainly causes urinary tract infection and gastroenteritis, and is only a minor cause of osteomyelitis, mostly in neonates and in the elderly.

questions.text: Presence of yellow honey crusted crumbs is strongly associated with:
questions.explanation: Non bullous impetigo (B) is correct because it is the commonest form of impetigo (caused by Staphylococcus aureus or group A streptococci): small vesicles or pustules burst quickly and dry into the typical honey-coloured (golden yellow) crusts, mainly around the nose and mouth. Bullous impetigo (A) is incorrect because it forms large, flaccid, fluid-filled blisters that leave a thin brown crust or a 'collarette' of skin. Scalded skin syndrome (C) is incorrect because it causes widespread redness, skin tenderness and sheet-like peeling of the skin with a positive Nikolsky's sign. Cellulitis (D) is incorrect because it is a deep spreading infection with warm, red, painful swollen skin, but without honey-coloured crusts.

questions.text: A pathophysiologic factor that contributes to the formation of esophageal varices is:

options.C: Decreased albumin formation by the liver

questions.explanation: Portal hypertension (B) is correct because in cirrhosis the scarred liver blocks the flow of portal blood, so the pressure in the portal vein rises, and blood is diverted through collateral veins at the lower oesophagus and the stomach, which dilate into thin-walled varices that can rupture and bleed massively. Increased central venous pressure (A) is incorrect because it is a feature of right-sided heart failure and fluid overload, and it is not the cause of varices. Decreased albumin formation by the liver (C) is incorrect because it causes ascites and oedema through a fall in oncotic pressure. Decreased prothrombin formation (D) is incorrect because it prolongs clotting and worsens the bleeding, but it does not form the varices.

questions.text: Priority nursing management for the pre-operative client with gastric cancer scheduled for partial gastroectomy include:
questions.explanation: Correction of nutritional deficits (B) is correct because patients with gastric cancer are usually malnourished and anaemic (from anorexia, vomiting, bleeding and weight loss), and poor nutrition delays wound healing, raises the risk of infection and anastomotic leakage, so the nurse corrects it before surgery with a high-protein, high-calorie diet, supplements, enteral or parenteral feeding, correction of anaemia and fluid and electrolyte balance. Discharge planning (A) is incorrect because it is begun on admission but is not the priority before surgery. Prevention of DVT (C) is incorrect because it is an important post-operative measure but is not the main pre-operative priority in this patient. Instruction regarding radiation treatment (D) is incorrect because radiation is not the planned treatment here, and any adjuvant therapy is discussed after surgery.

questions.text: Terminal sedation in palliative care involves:

options.A: Administration of medications to keep patients pain free
options.B: Keeping patients in unconscious state until they die
options.C: Administering pain relief medications that end up hastening death
options.D: Provision of knowledge to a patient to terminate life

questions.explanation: Keeping patients in unconscious state until they die (B) is correct because terminal (palliative) sedation is the use of sedative drugs (for example midazolam) to lower the level of consciousness of a dying patient, up to unconsciousness, when symptoms such as agitation, breathlessness or pain cannot be controlled by any other means, and the sedation is continued until death occurs naturally. Administration of medications to keep patients pain free (A) is incorrect because it describes ordinary analgesia, which is not aimed at reducing consciousness. Administering pain relief medications that end up hastening death (C) is incorrect because it describes the 'double effect' ethical principle, where death is an unintended consequence, and it is not the definition of sedation. Provision of knowledge to a patient to terminate life (D) is incorrect because it describes assisted suicide, which is illegal in Kenya. Note: definitions of palliative sedation differ slightly between textbooks, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: An Appropriate incision for an exploratory laparotomy in an 8-year child is:
questions.explanation: Transverse (C) is correct because in infants and young children the abdominal cavity is wide and short, so a transverse (horizontal) incision gives good access with a lower risk of wound dehiscence and a better scar, and it is the standard incision in paediatric abdominal surgery. Kocher's incision (A) is incorrect because it is a right subcostal incision used in adults for gallbladder and biliary surgery. Midline (B) is incorrect as the best answer because it is the usual incision for exploratory laparotomy in adults, and it is used in children only for a major emergency or when wide access is needed. McBurney's (D) is incorrect because it is a small right iliac fossa muscle-splitting incision for appendicectomy. Note: some sources accept a midline incision in children, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: The priority nursing intervention for a patient who has just been brought to the Post Anaesthetic Care Unit (PACU) is:

options.A: Check the dressing for bleeding, ensure infusion is running well
options.B: Ensure drains and tubes are patent, position the patient
options.D: Assess vital signs and limb observations, keep patient warm

questions.explanation: Maintain patent airway, administer oxygen (C) is correct because the airway comes first in the ABC priority: the patient is still under the effect of anaesthetic drugs, the tongue can fall back, secretions or vomit can block the airway, and hypoxia can develop, so the nurse positions the patient (head tilt, jaw thrust or side-lying), suctions as needed and gives oxygen before any other care. Check the dressing for bleeding and ensure infusion is running well (A), ensure drains and tubes are patent and position the patient (B) and assess vital signs and limb observations and keep the patient warm (D) are incorrect as the first priority because they are important but come after the airway and breathing are secured.

questions.text: The class of anti-emetics effective in the treatment of nausea due to cytotoxic agent is:
questions.explanation: Serotonin receptor antagonist (D) is correct because cytotoxic drugs release serotonin (5-HT3) from the gut lining, which stimulates the vomiting centre and the chemoreceptor trigger zone, and 5-HT3 blockers such as ondansetron, granisetron and palonosetron are the most effective drugs for chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (often combined with dexamethasone). Antihistamines (A) are incorrect because they (for example promethazine and cinnarizine) are used in motion sickness and vestibular nausea. Anticholinergics (B) are incorrect because drugs such as hyoscine are used for motion sickness and colic. Prokinetics (C) are incorrect because metoclopramide and domperidone speed gastric emptying and are used for gastric stasis and reflux, and are less effective for chemotherapy-induced vomiting.

questions.text: A class of drugs that lowers blood sugar by stimulating the pancreatic cells to secrete insulin:
questions.explanation: Meglitinides (A) are correct because drugs such as repaglinide and nateglinide close the potassium channels of the pancreatic beta cells and stimulate a quick, short release of insulin at mealtimes (like the sulphonylureas, which are the other secretagogue class). Thiazolidinediones (B) are incorrect because pioglitazone makes the tissues more sensitive to insulin (reduces insulin resistance). Biguanides (C) are incorrect because metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and improves insulin sensitivity, and it does not stimulate insulin release. Alpha-glucosidase inhibitors (D) are incorrect because acarbose delays the digestion and absorption of carbohydrate in the gut.

questions.text: An example of an antimuscarinic agent is:
questions.explanation: Atropine sulphate (A) is correct because it blocks the muscarinic receptors of acetylcholine, which raises the heart rate, dilates the pupils, dries secretions and relaxes smooth muscle (other antimuscarinics are hyoscine and ipratropium). Methimazole (B) is incorrect because it is an antithyroid drug that blocks the synthesis of thyroid hormones. Propranolol (C) is incorrect because it is a non-selective beta blocker. Captopril (D) is incorrect because it is an ACE inhibitor used in hypertension and heart failure.

questions.text: The agent of choice in the treatment of opioid overdose is:
questions.explanation: Naloxone (C) is correct because it is a pure opioid receptor antagonist that quickly reverses the respiratory depression, pinpoint pupils and coma of an opioid overdose (given IV, IM or intranasally, and repeated because its effect is shorter than that of most opioids). Flumazenil (A) is incorrect because it is the antidote for benzodiazepine overdose. Acetylcysteine (B) is incorrect because it is the antidote for paracetamol overdose. Glucagon (D) is incorrect because it treats severe hypoglycaemia and beta-blocker overdose.

questions.text: The drug of choice is the management of psychotic features is:
questions.explanation: Haloperidol, Olanzapine (B) is correct because both are antipsychotics that block dopamine D2 receptors and treat hallucinations, delusions and agitation, haloperidol being a typical (first generation) drug and olanzapine an atypical (second generation) drug. Olanzapine, chlordiazepoxide (A) is incorrect because chlordiazepoxide is a benzodiazepine used for anxiety and alcohol withdrawal, and not for psychosis. Disulfiram, flumazenil (C) is incorrect because disulfiram is an alcohol-aversion drug and flumazenil is a benzodiazepine antagonist. Haloperidol, methadone (D) is incorrect because methadone is an opioid used as a substitute in opioid dependence.

questions.text: One of the following is contradicted in children:
questions.explanation: Tetracyclines (C) are correct because they bind calcium in developing bones and teeth, so in pregnancy and in children under 8 years they cause permanent yellow-brown discolouration of teeth, enamel hypoplasia and temporary slowing of bone growth. Cephalosporins (A) are incorrect because they are widely used and safe in children. Aminoglycosides (B) are incorrect because gentamicin is used in children and neonates with dose adjustment and monitoring for kidney and hearing damage, and it is not contraindicated. Sulphonamides (D) are incorrect as the answer because they are used in children (for example co-trimoxazole), and are only avoided in newborns in the first weeks of life, because of the risk of kernicterus.

questions.text: The following adverse effects is characterized by need for increasing dosage:
questions.explanation: Tolerance (D) is correct because it is the state in which the body gets used to a drug with repeated use, so a larger dose is needed to produce the same effect (for example with opioids and benzodiazepines). Teratogenicity (A) is incorrect because it is the capacity of a drug to cause malformations in the fetus. Dependency (B) is incorrect because it is the physical or psychological need to continue taking the drug, with withdrawal symptoms on stopping, which often follows tolerance but does not itself mean that the dose has to rise. Idiosyncrasy (C) is incorrect because it is an unusual, unpredictable reaction to a drug, often from a genetic difference, which is not related to the dose.

questions.text: The study of drugs vegetables and animal origin is referred to as:
questions.explanation: Pharmacognosy (C) is correct because it is the study of drugs obtained from natural sources, such as plants (for example digoxin from foxglove and morphine from the poppy), animals and minerals. Pharmacotherapeutics (A) is incorrect because it is the use of drugs to prevent and treat disease. Pharmacodynamics (B) is incorrect because it is the study of what the drug does to the body (its mechanism and effects). Clinical pharmacology (D) is incorrect because it is the study of the effects of drugs in humans, including the evaluation of their safety and efficacy.

questions.text: Secondary sites targeted by mumps virus after dissemination include:
questions.explanation: Testicles, pancreas (A) is correct because after the mumps virus multiplies in the parotid glands it spreads through the blood to other glandular tissue and the central nervous system, and the commonest secondary sites are the testes (orchitis in post-pubertal males, which can reduce fertility), the pancreas (pancreatitis), the meninges (aseptic meningitis), and less often the ovaries, the ear and the thyroid. Liver, lungs (B), spleen, lungs (C) and ovaries, liver (D) are incorrect because the lungs, spleen and liver are not target organs of the mumps virus, and ovarian involvement (oophoritis) is much less common than orchitis.

questions.text: An infant is noted to have a temperature of 39.7°C during triage. Appropriate action is to:

options.A: Administer per rectal paracetamol stat dose and instruct the mother to take child for consultation
options.B: Instruct mother to loosen infant’s clothing and continue following the queue
options.C: Remove all the infant’s clothing and shout for help
options.D: Take the infant to emergency room and repeat the temperature measurement

questions.explanation: Administer per rectal paracetamol stat dose and instruct the mother to take child for consultation (A) is correct as the best answer because a temperature of 39.7 degrees Celsius is a high fever that must be lowered quickly to prevent febrile convulsions and discomfort, so the triage nurse gives a stat antipyretic, which can be given rectally if the child cannot take oral medicine, and the child is then sent for urgent consultation to find the cause. Instruct mother to loosen infant's clothing and continue following the queue (B) is incorrect because the child with a high fever must not wait in the queue. Remove all the infant's clothing and shout for help (C) is incorrect because it is an exaggerated reaction, and exposure can cause chilling. Take the infant to emergency room and repeat the temperature measurement (D) is incorrect because it delays treatment, and the fever is treated first. Note: option D is defensible if the infant shows danger signs, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: Insertion of nasogastric tube in a child diagnosed with acute abdomen is to:
questions.explanation: Decompress the stomach (C) is correct because in an acute abdomen (for example intestinal obstruction or peritonitis) the stomach and bowel fill with fluid and gas, and a nasogastric tube left on free drainage or gentle suction empties the stomach, relieves distension and vomiting, lowers the risk of aspiration, and keeps the stomach empty for surgery. Commence enteral feeding (A) is incorrect because the child is kept nil by mouth when there is a possible need for surgery. Perform gastric lavage (B) is incorrect because lavage is used in poisoning. Obtain gastric contents for investigations (D) is incorrect because it is a minor, secondary use of the tube.
